ZONDO ARRESTS: JUSTICE DELAYED

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
With the first Zondo Commission arrests happening this week - it's a sign of hope for the country. The wheels of Justice are finally turning.

Unique Selling Point:
A story CB can claim - followed from the start in 2012 up to now

Summary:
With the first Zondo Commission arrests happening this week - it's a sign of hope for the country. The wheels of Justice are finally turning.

We take a quick look at the arrests and then hone in on the Durban Death Squad // Thoshan Panday debacle.



Further information:
It’s been 8 years we did the first story on the so-called Durban Death Squad. We did an expose on Thosan Panday in 2016 and the failure of authorities to arrest him. We did an exclusive interview with Major General Johan Booysen who was at the centre of the Death Squad / Panday controversy and even touched on it in the 2017 NPA farce piece.

Thosan Panday and his accomplice Col Madhoe have been arrested and charged. Today another police official and the then KZN Provincial Commissioner, Ngobeni are said to hand themselves over.

Advocate Jiba has been removed and discredited. Shaun Abrahams is gone. Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions Noko is under investigation. Phiyega is long gone.

The journalists at the centre of the articles that kick started the witch hunt have been discredited and have handed back awards they received for the series of articles. They have also been slated in Anton Harber’s new book.

We’ve been on the story since it broke. I think it’s worth a follow up to claim some of the credit – we were telling the right story all along. After Booysen’s Zondo commission testimony and constant criticism of the NPA inability to take action – the wheels of justice have finally started turning.

It’s a story that disrupted the lives of 26 policemen – all because of corruption at the hands of Thosand Panday – it’s taken 8 years for the right people to be arrested.

This story ties in with the Zondo arrests, it gives hope that good will overcome evil.

STRUCTURE: Justice Better Late Than Never

VO: Time is running out for those implicated in corruption – as the HAWKS and National Prosecuting Authority’s investigations close in on suspects, across the country.

LINK: Over the past two weeks South Africa has seen more arrests of high-profile people linked to state capture and grand corruption than we have seen over the past two decades. It seems the wheels of justice are finally in motion.

RALPH: It is just nearly impossible for any politician to stop this. It is out of their control.

VO: Policital Anaylyst Ralph Matekga explains these arrests are a move in the right direction.

RALPH: The thing is that corruption is so complex even within the ANC because of the political consequences and the backlash. They cannot control these cases it has become inevitable that these cases have to be prosecuted.

VO: First stop - the Free State. The Case: THE ASBESTOS DEAL.

It’s centred around a R255-million, Free State Department of Human Settlements contract, for the audit of asbestos roofing in more than 35000 homes that was awarded in 2014.

Carte Blanche exposed this scandal in 2019.

UPSOUND APRIL 2019
V/O (Devi): The brazenness is best understood here on these dusty streets where some homes still have harmful asbestos roofs.

MXOLISI DUKWANA: “You’re doing this for the poor, it’s 2019. These people are still staying in the same houses.”
DEVI: “So where was the emergency?”
MXOLISI DUKWANA: “R255 million is gone… it was an emergency to steal”

VO: Fast Forward to September 2020 and seven of the alleged masterminds behind this lucrative deal were arrested.

Businessmen Sello Radebe, Abel Manyeki and Edwin Sodi along with former government officials Nthimotse Mokhesi, Thabane Zulu, Mahlomola Matlakala and ousted Manguang mayor Olly Mlamleli face 60 criminal charges including corruption, fraud and money laundering.

The cabal allegedly made off with at least R200 million in profit. The Asset Forfeiture Unit’s seizures has cast the spotlight on the lavish lifestyles of the accused.

And this, is just the tip of the iceberg feels Paul Hoffman, from Accountability Now.

HOFFMAN: Corruption is not a crime that takes place in the open. The victims often don't even know that they are victims of of the crime. It is often well concealed.

VO: Next up: Gauteng. The Case: Bosasa

The alleged corrupt activities, of a billion rand facilities management business, became the focus of the Zondo Commission, when former COO – corruptor turned whistlblower, Angelo Agrizzi testified. He detailed how exactly the company scored government contracts – that raked in at least R2.8 billion over the past decade.

In an exclusive interview in 2019, Agrizzi opened up about the web of corruption involving high-ranking government officials, members of parliament and NPA staff.

UPSOUND CARTE BLANCHE JANUARY 2019
d – anything legit
a – salaries and wages paid on time
d – that’s it?
A – that’s all – there’s nothing that’s legitimate – all smokes and mirrors

VO: Last week Agrizzi was charged with corruption alongside former top ANC MP Vincent Smith for two payments of over 600 thousand rand (R671k) made to Smith’s company Euro Blitz. In addition, Smith will face charges of fraud for not declaring the benefits to Parliament.

HOFFMAN: The people who are being charged now are the ones who are expendable - they are not the ones who have the political connections to prevent them from being held accountable for what they have done wrong that enable them to continue almost seamlessly with the culture of impunity for corrupt activity.

VO: NPA Spokesperson for the Investigating Directorate, Sindisiwe Twala, explains starting at the bottom is part of their strategy.

TWALA: you need to start from the people who aided or facilitated or were the hands that were used in order to get the funds looted. We are building our way up in order to find out what exactly happened.
MASA Without naming names – are there more arrests on the cards?
TWALA: This is the beginning of people seeing the culmination of various investigations

LINK: But these arrests call for cautious optimism – the fight against state capture and corruption has kicked off – but arrests are just the starting point, the criminal justice system will now have to step up and deliver successful prosecutions.

RALPH: in all fairness some of these cases could be easily be prosecuted by law students. They are low hanging fruit when it comes to the facts. They are not sophisticated that what I call pedestrian corruption.

VO: Matekga explains, the perfect example is the last of batch of arrests.

KwaZulu Natal. The Case: The 2010 World Cup Police Accommodation Deal.

The Arrests: Businessman Thoshan Panday, police Colonel Navin Madhoe, Captain Aswin Narainpershad and former KZN police commissioner Mmamonnye Ngobeni.

It’s a story we started investigating in 2012.

VO: The seemingly untouchable Durban Billionaire Thoshan Panday was implicated in three cases – alleged tender fraud of R60 million, police corruption of a further 15 million and R1.3 million bribery case. Central to these investigations – former police Major General Johan Booysen.

In 2012 we exposed the alleged bribery of Major General Booysen with this footage. Colonel Madhoe is seen here placing a suitcase said to contain R1-point-three million in cash, into Booysen’s boot, in exchange for his help, to make the original case against Panday – go away.

While Madhoe declined to comment. Thoshan Panday has previously insisted there was no evidence against him and denied all allegations. Although police insiders claimed the proof was there.

UPSOUND UNTOUCHABLE PANDAY
INSIDER: R1.3 million rand is // a lot of notes and //in the bundles there were deposit slips and these deposits slips found in the money indicated that it was withdrawn from an account linked to Thoshan Panday.

VO: Panday has been known to brag about his contacts.

This clip is from our 2016 story. Panday is talking about invoices.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER UNTOUCHABLE PANDAY
PANDAY: sort it out, I’ll hand it over to he Minister and he’ll authorised payment immediately…

VO: Panday declined an interview via his attorney saying the case was still before court and.... “Our client is presently in the process of seeking leave to appeal against the decision to prosecute him in the 2010 football World Cup matter. Our client trusts that his right to be presumed innocent will be respected during these processes and that the law is allowed to take its course.”

Hoffman is not surprised that these types of cases have been delayed.

HOFFMAN: The politically connected people and people high up in the governing alliance have enjoyed impunity against prosecution because they have have been treated as royal game by the hollowed out criminal justice administration.

VO: A fact the NPA doesn’t deny.

TWALA: Thoshan Panday case had a lot of political influence and interference interference of all sorts in many of these cases which do not make sense why they were halted.

VO: But the interference came with collateral damage.

Before the Panday investigations could be finalised in 2012, despite video, documentary and cellphone evidence – General Booysen would be arrested, charged and suspended – actions he believes were linked to the Panday investigations.

He was charged along with 27 members of the Cato Manor Organised Crime Unit. Labelled a death squad – the unit faced 116 charges, and stood accused of the planting of weapons, racketeering and murder. This, after a series of photographs were leaked to the press.

BOOYSEN: there never was a death squad it was a narrative created by individuals who had an agenda of their own.

VO: In 2018 the Sunday Times retracted the articles and published an apology.

Then, in July 2019 all charges were withdrawn against Booysen and the so-called Durban Death Squad.

Hoffman believes the NPA failed in their duties in the prosecution of the Booysen matter.

HOFFMAN: Instead of serving the people of South Africa without fear or favour or prejudice operatives within the NPA were serving their political masters the people who appointed them expected them to look after them.

VO: Booysen agrees. He points out that while the Panday evidence was available to the NPA for years, he and the Cato Manor unit were persecuted.

BOOYSEN: These nothing as blind as those who do not want to see. Under the. Leadership of Jiba at the National Prosecuting Authority. And later with Sean Abrams and they were in my view. Clearly compromised.

VO: Although both Jiba and Abrahams have left the NPA and criminal investigations have been instituted against them - Jiba stands by her decision to prosecute Booysen and the unit.

Abrahams wrote: : “I dispute any insinuation or assertion that I had conspired with other members of the National Prosecuting Authority [NPA] to institute prosecutions against any person(s).”

He added “all decisions I made were not informed by any improper motive or influences by anyone and were made without fear, favour or prejudice .”

Twala says the NPA has taken stock and are busy cleaning house.

TWALA: we're not blind to the fact that as much as the investigating Directorate is a new entity or a new unit in order to fight corruption. However the system has not completely been rid of persons who aided. By corruption or the capture in the security sector. So we need to be guarded.

VO: But it’s too early to pop the champagne as there is still a huge moral backlog in dealing with corruption warns Matekga.

RALPH: The NPA has to try to end back its legitimacy. All of this is going to test as to whether we can say that justice in South Africa does look nor any political affiliation. Does not know power.

VO: Others are more optimistic about the message that these arrests send.

BOOYSEN: if you're busy with corruption now I want to tell you somewhere along the line it's going to catch up with you.



PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: With a string of crucial state capture and grand corruption linked arrests in recent weeks – we ask if this a turning a point for South Africa, as the wheels of justice finally start turning.

PROMO 2
VO: Despite video, documentary and cellphone evidence dating back almost a decade – arrests are now only materialising years later in the multi-million rand police accommodation fraud scheme.

PROMO 3
VO: After a flurry of arrests in KZN, Gauteng and the Free State - criminals suspects linked to grand corruption and state capture land up in the dock. We ask why it’s taken so long?

metadata.Further information: It’s been 8 years we did the first story on the so-called Durban Death Squad. We did an expose on Thosan Panday in 2016 and the failure of authorities to arrest him. We did an exclusive interview with Major General Johan Booysen who was at the centre of the Death Squad / Panday controversy and even touched on it in the 2017 NPA farce piece. Thosan Panday and his accomplice Col Madhoe have been arrested and charged. Today another police official and the then KZN Provincial Commissioner, Ngobeni are said to hand themselves over. Advocate Jiba has been removed and discredited. Shaun Abrahams is gone. Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions Noko is under investigation. Phiyega is long gone. The journalists at the centre of the articles that kick started the witch hunt have been discredited and have handed back awards they received for the series of articles. They have also been slated in Anton Harber’s new book. We’ve been on the story since it broke. I think it’s worth a follow up to claim some of the credit – we were telling the right story all along. After Booysen’s Zondo commission testimony and constant criticism of the NPA inability to take action – the wheels of justice have finally started turning. It’s a story that disrupted the lives of 26 policemen – all because of corruption at the hands of Thosand Panday – it’s taken 8 years for the right people to be arrested. This story ties in with the Zondo arrests, it gives hope that good will overcome evil. INTERVIEWS: - JOHAN BOOYSEN - PAUL HOFFMAN - ACCOUNTABILITY NOW - NPA
